questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I wanted to study at a good university where there were good opportunities for traveling and seeing beautiful nature.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer:
Going on exchange was absolutely amazing.
Though be aware that the term seems a bit short. Classes from September until early December and then exams in December and everything is done before Christmas.
The academic level seemed pretty easy compared to KU.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was manageable but there were times where I had to reach out and spend a lot of time searching their whole homepage trying to find some info I felt I was missing.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: Upon arrival we basically got a key to the room and a one-pages with a bit of basic info. We had an introduction day to see the school which was okay but it was a mix of students from all majors so I never saw any of them again afterwards.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: I was at first assigned a room in a shared apartment with 3 other people. I managed to do a room switch with someone else after a few days so I ended up with a single room which was amazing.

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: The meal plan depends on which building you are living in. I didn't have a meal plan but had my own kitchen with pretty good cooking facilities.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
questions.answer: The single room I got was a full apartment which was amazing. I think it's rare to get the single room I was lucky to get.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer:
I think we were very unlucky in terms of registration as they were migrating from their old system to a new system (Workday).
Therefore it felt very last minute before I got to see which classes were being offered for the term.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: We had to fill out something similar to a google form and then the exchange team would try to add you to classes. I was only added to 3 classes as it was full time so had to reach out and be allowed to be added to a 4th class. As exchange students don't fulfill any prerequisites it was not possible to add any classes on my own initially. After taking to them a few times they removed the prerequisites from 3 classes so I would be able to add myself to one of them if a spot became available.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer:
The exchange team (GoGlobal) were happy to help but the initial setup where you have to reach out and hope they can add you to a class before it's full was not a very efficient process.
The course descriptions is nearly non existing for the classes (just 3 lines) so you have to reach out to each professor and ask for a course syllabus. All professors were very quick at replying.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Somewhat succesfull. I got my 2nd, 5th, 8th and 10th priority. I was not possible to get classes from other faculties.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Start with the pre-approval of courses as early as possible. If they remove pre-requisites for some classes so you can add yourself then check frequently and be fast as it's first come, first serve.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer:
The level was easy compared to KU.
Basically it's impossible to fail a course even with mediocre effort.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer:
Each lecture was 1 hour and 20 minutes with no breaks. Only one class had exercise/lab but it was 1 hour of going through the first 3 questions out of the roughly 12 questions for the assignment for the following week. I had already finished the assignment before the exercise class so I only attended the first one.
They have office hours where you can talk to prof or TA every week if you have questions.
You will have 1 or 2 midterm exams during the term and then 1 final exam. Many classes have assignments that counts for some of the grade and you will also get a few points for participation.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Econ 221 - introduction to strategic thinking with Hao Li (pre-approved as Micro 3).
The class was very easy in terms of the math. He can seem a bit confusing and on ratemyprof he gets very low rating for the class. He also teaches game theory at a 400 level (421) which is basically the same class but assume students can do more math where he gets very good rating. I recommend taking the 400 level if possible.

Econ 333 - Economic History of Europe from the Paleolithic to the Industrial Revolution with Mauricio Drelichman (pre-approves as Økonomish Historie).
Absolutely amazing class. Mauricio is a fantastic story-teller and makes the classes super interesting. One of the best professors and best classes I have ever had.

Econ 356 - Introduction to International Finance with Emrul Hasan (økonomisk valfag).
The class is similar to Economics of Exchange rates from KU. He added a bit of portfolio theory in the end. He seems very interested in making it relevant to what we will experience and likes to give career advice. Very engaging professor.

Econ 441 - The Process of Economic Development with Filipe Caicedo (pre-approved as Development Economics)
Interesting class on inequality and examples of relatively small things to improve developing nations.

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
Econ 333 - Economic History of Europe from the Paleolithic to the Industrial Revolution with Mauricio Drelichman is an absolutely must take.
He is an economic historian so some of the papers for the classes are things he wrote. He is very passionate about the topic and tells about how some of the "behind the scenes" for some of the papers as he is often giving peer feedback on several of the papers before they are published. He is an amazing story teller and the class is an absolute joy. I wish I could have more classes with him.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: I don't think I had any unexpected costs.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: The food was more expensive than expected. Groceries were more expensive than Denmark.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: They were updating their homepage so it was a little difficult to learn all about the clubs in the beginning and 4 months is a bit short to really join them.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: They had a crazy amount of clubs for almost anything imaginable and lots of recreational facilities, including a large indoor pool.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: They have a lot of amazing nature in Canada. Go on all the trips you can to Vancouver Island, Whistler, Banff etc.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Go hiking or skiing. The time passes super fast.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: I felt like there was no adjustment needed, it was very easy to get along with everyone.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Join clubs or other social activities. It's almost impossible to get to know people through the classes.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: None.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: A lot of them are outdoor people and are happy to go hiking or give recommendations for where to go.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Enjoy it and take advantage of the wonderful nature. Try to do things on your weekends to get out.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: N/A

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Amazing nature and got a few close friends.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Getting to do all the things I wanted to do. I felt like I almost just arrived and then had to leave again. Would have loved to stay for 2 terms.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: N/A

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
